chunks: And Abul Qasim (peace be upon him) was among the most intelligent of people in the view of both the opposing and the agreeing parties, and he practiced dissimulation (Taqiyyah).

key_terms.أَبو الْقَاسِمِ: Abul Qasim, a title for Husain bin Rauh
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: Taqiyyah, the practice of dissimulation or concealing one's faith/beliefs to avoid harm
key_terms.الْمُخَالِفِ: The opposing party (often referring to Sunnis or political rivals)
key_terms.وَالْمُوَافِقِ: The agreeing party (often referring to Shias or allies)

ai.seo_question: Who was Abul Qasim and what was his reputation for intelligence and Taqiyyah?
ai.summary: This note from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores Abul Qasim Husain bin Rauh’s exceptional intellect, which commanded respect across sectarian lines, while highlighting his strategic use of *Taqiyyah* as a vital tool for preserving religious identity during periods of political pressure. This practice is not merely concealment but a nuanced application of wisdom, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing truth with prudence in the face of opposition.
